confirmed: source.version is exact: the PDF is the published AHFE International paper, Human Factors in Training, Education, and Learning Sciences, Vol. 231, 2026, pp. 141-149, doi 10.54941/ahfe1008005, received Nov 5, 2025, accepted Apr 23, 2026, online Jul 20, 2026. The footer also lists Revised April 5, 2026, which the form omits without harm (PDF p. 1 header and footer; Crossref confirms title, volume 231, and DOI).
Title, author order (Xue Xia, Bote Qi, Shuting Jin), and page count (9) match the document. Crossref lists Xia, Jin, Qi, and the form correctly follows the PDF (PDF p. 1).

The paper mentions no supplement, appendix, preregistration, data or code link, funding, or company role, so supplement not_stated, preregistered not_stated, and the empty company and data fields are right (whole PDF, text-layer search).

Random assignment is stated twice: 'randomly assigned to three conditions' (PDF p. 2, printed p. 142, Introduction) and 'Participants were randomly assigned to one of three experimental conditions, with 15 students in each group.' (PDF p. 3, printed p. 143, Methods). The abstract says only 'divided', which explains the triage value not_stated.

Counts are people: 45 industrial design undergraduates from one university, 14 females and 31 males, 15 per arm. The country is not stated, so the empty field is right. participants.quote and assignment.quote are verbatim (PDF p. 3, printed p. 143).

n_analyzed 45 (15 per arm) is supported: Figure 1 says 'Stage 1: 45 students engaged in the design task', 'Each student produced an A3 marker sketch', and the experts 'independently evaluated all sketches'. No exclusions are reported. 45 people across all arms is below 50 (PDF pp. 3-5, printed pp. 143-145).

Arms and AI coding are right: G1 no external tools (none), G2 Pinterest image search (other_aid), G3 Midjourney (generative_ai, role image_generation). G2 and G3 got a short standardized training and kept process logs, and researchers monitored compliance on site (PDF p. 3, printed p. 143).
Task is right: a cognitive training wooden toy for older adults, 160 minutes, one annotated A3 marker sketch per student, coded design_visual (PDF p. 3, printed p. 143).

Ratings: ten experts with industrial design experience, blind to group, scored all sketches on four five-point dimensions, analyzed with 'Descriptive statistics and Friedman tests (SPSS 30)'. No means, SDs, test statistics, or p-values are printed anywhere, so figure_only is right (PDF p. 5, printed p. 145; text-layer search).
All three 'reported' quotes are verbatim, and their locators, PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 145-146), are right.

Directions for G3 vs G1 are right: higher on originality and effectiveness, lower on feasibility and usability. Bar lengths in Figure 3, measured in memory (not printed in the paper), give the same order (PDF p. 6, printed p. 146).

Constructs fit the codebook: originality is novelty, and effectiveness and feasibility are usefulness. question with_ai, timing immediate, and AI available are right. primary not_stated is right because the paper names no primary outcome.

unit output is consistent with the paper treating each student's sketch and process record as 'a single analysis unit' (PDF p. 4, printed p. 144). The paper does not say how its Friedman tests were blocked, as the form notes, and n_units null is right.

Eligibility is right: design_class lab_rct (supervised, on site), criterion 1 met, criterion 2 not met (45 people across all arms), criterion 3 met, core no, context_class none (PDF p. 3, printed p. 143).

The homogenization claim appears only in the abstract. The body supports it with qualitative evidence, such as student reports that 'Pinterest often produced visually similar clusters'. No diversity measure across people is computed (PDF p. 1 and p. 6, printed pp. 141 and 146).
one_line_finding's rank statements and its '15 students per arm' match the text (PDF p. 3 and p. 5). Only its 'unlabeled bar chart' wording needs the fix above.
summary: The full published PDF supports the form's core reading: 45 industrial design students were randomly assigned, 15 per arm, to no tool, Pinterest, or Midjourney, and blind experts rated each sketch, so this is a small randomized experiment that fails only the 50-person criterion, and every quote, count, and direction checks out. Three fixes are needed: usability needs its own outcome, each outcome lacks the Midjourney-versus-Pinterest (ai_vs_active) contrast that the text ranks, and the form calls the Figure 3 bars 'group means' in an 'unlabeled' chart although the paper names no statistic and the chart lacks only value labels.
